questions.question: What color are warning signs with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: A person's body removes about one drink per hour. Someone drinks 7 drinks in 3 hours. How many drinks are likely still in their system 3 hours after their last drink?
questions.correctAnswerText: Four
questions.explanation: To find how many drinks remain, subtract the hours since the last drink from total drinks consumed. A person who drinks 7 drinks in 3 hours would have about 4 drinks left in their system 3 hours later.

questions.question: Smoothly downshifting on motorcycles:

options.text: Can help slow the bike by using engine braking.
Should not be done when other vehicles are nearby.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can help slow the bike by using engine braking.
questions.explanation: Engine braking through smooth downshifting is useful for motorcyclists. Use your brake lights separately to tell other drivers you are slowing down.

questions.question: Space around your motorcycle helps you to:
questions.correctAnswerText: React quickly to dangers.
questions.explanation: Keep space around your motorcycle at all times. This gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake and lets you maneuver safely.

questions.question: When someone tailgates you, you should:

options.text: Ignore them and focus on the road ahead.
Change lanes and let them pass.
Ride on the shoulder and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up makes it more dangerous. Never ride on the shoulder because drivers will not expect you there.

questions.question: To control your motorcycle well, you should:

options.text: Use your arms to prop yourself up instead of steering.
Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance.
Let your feet hang off the footrests.
Sit far back and stretch to reach the handgrips.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance.
questions.explanation: Keep your knees against the gas tank to maintain balance in turns. Sit forward enough that your arms are slightly bent at the handgrips. Keep your feet firmly on the footrests.

questions.question: To stop quickly, the best method is to:

options.text: Release the throttle and use the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Is not needed if you have a windshield.
Does not protect your face as well as goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protects your entire face.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not a good substitute for a face shield or goggles.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, you should NOT:
questions.correctAnswerText: Brake suddenly.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, slow down, avoid sudden movements, and use both brakes gently if you need to brake.

questions.question: After mounting your motorcycle, you should do everything EXCEPT:

options.text: Check that the mirrors are clean.
Check that the clutch works smoothly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close the fuel supply valve.
questions.explanation: After mounting, check that the clutch, throttle, horn, and brakes all work. Clean and adjust the mirrors. Make sure the fuel supply valve is OPEN.

questions.question: Where do motorcycles have the greatest risk of conflict with other traffic?
questions.correctAnswerText: Intersections
questions.explanation: Intersections are where motorcycles face the greatest risk of conflict with other traffic. Stay alert at intersections because other vehicles may cross in front of you.

questions.question: When adjusting your mirrors, what should you see?

options.text: The road behind and to the side of your motorcycle.
The road in front of your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road behind and to the side of your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors to see the lane behind you and as much of the lane next to you as possible. You may see the edge of your arm or shoulder, but seeing the road behind and to the side is most important.

questions.question: What does making eye contact with a driver mean?

options.text: The driver will let you go.
The driver may not actually see you.
It is a waste of time.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver may not actually see you.
questions.explanation: Do not rely on eye contact to know that a driver sees you. A driver may look directly at you and still not notice you.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield do?

options.text: It is not needed if you have a windshield.
Goggles protect better than a face shield.

questions.correctAnswerText: It protects your whole face.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your whole face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not a substitute for a face shield or goggles.

questions.question: When being passed, which of these is NOT a hazard?

options.text: Objects being thrown from other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Headlights.
questions.explanation: When being passed, watch out for the passing vehicle's mirrors, wind from the vehicle, and objects thrown by passengers. Headlights are not a hazard when being passed.

questions.question: What is true about the front brake?

options.text: Use it only when you need to stop quickly.
Use it only on slippery roads.
It is not as good as the rear brake.
It is safe to use if you use it correctly.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is safe to use if you use it correctly.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes any time you slow down or stop. The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake and is safe when used correctly.

questions.question: What does eye contact with a driver guarantee?

options.text: The driver will properly yield to you.
It is a waste of time.
It does not guarantee the driver will yield to you.
The driver knows you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not guarantee the driver will yield to you.
questions.explanation: Never assume that eye contact means a driver will properly yield the right-of-way to you.

questions.question: What can happen if you brake too hard?

options.text: You lose traction on one or both wheels.

questions.correctAnswerText: You lose traction on one or both wheels.
questions.explanation: Braking too hard can cause you to lose traction on one or both wheels, which can lead to a crash.

questions.question: What is true when passing another vehicle?

options.text: Complete the pass without exceeding the speed limit.
You can finish a pass in a no passing zone if you started it before.
You may exceed the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Complete the pass without exceeding the speed limit.
questions.explanation: All passes must be done at the posted speed limit and only where passing is allowed.

questions.question: When a group of motorcyclists passes a vehicle on a two-lane road, how should they pass?

options.text: Pass in a staggered formation with several riders at once.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pass one at a time.
questions.explanation: When a group of motorcyclists passes a vehicle on a two-lane road, each rider should pass one at a time. Wait until the pass is complete before the next rider begins.

questions.question: How should you stop quickly?

options.text: Use the front brake first, then the rear brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, press both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: How should you lean a motorcycle when turning?

options.text: Press the handgrip opposite to the direction of the turn.
Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: To turn a motorcycle, it must lean. Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn to make the motorcycle lean.

questions.question: What should a motorcyclist do when riding near stopped or slow-moving cars?

options.text: Pull over and wait for traffic to move.
Ride on the shoulder to pass quickly.
Weave between cars to pass quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not weave between cars.
questions.explanation: Weaving between stopped or parked cars is dangerous. Doors can open or cars can pull out suddenly. You will not have room to move safely. Never ride on the shoulder because other drivers will not expect you there.

questions.question: What type of sign is rectangular?
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are rectangular with white background and black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: When railroad tracks cross your lane at an angle, what is usually safest?

options.text: Ride straight in your lane to cross the tracks.
Ride straight in your lane to cross the tracks is dangerous.
It is not safe to cross tracks on a motorcycle.
Ride on the shoulder to cross the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride straight in your lane to cross the tracks.
questions.explanation: When tracks cross your lane at an angle, ride straight through your lane. Turning to cross at a 90-degree angle is dangerous because you could move into another lane of traffic.
